name: Barbell Bench Press
instructions: Lie flat on the bench with your eyes under the bar, feet planted on the floor, and a slight natural arch in your lower back.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder width, retract your shoulder blades, and unrack the bar so it sits over your chest with arms extended.
Lower the bar under control to your mid-chest (around the nipple line), keeping your elbows tucked at roughly a 45 to 75 degree angle to your torso.
Touch the chest lightly without bouncing, then press the bar back up and slightly toward your face until your arms are fully extended.
Lock out the rep, reset your breath, and repeat. Use a spotter or safety pins for heavy sets.
formCues: Keep your shoulder blades pinched and chest up throughout
Drive your feet into the floor for full-body tension
Wrap your thumb around the bar (no suicide grip)
commonMistakes: Bouncing the bar off the chest
Flaring the elbows out to 90 degrees and stressing the shoulders
Lifting the hips off the bench to cheat the weight up

name: Incline Barbell Bench Press
instructions: Set an adjustable bench to roughly a 30 to 45 degree incline and lie back with your eyes under the bar and feet flat on the floor.
Grip the bar slightly wider than shoulder width, retract your shoulder blades, and unrack the bar over your upper chest.
Lower the bar under control to the top of your chest, just below the collarbone, keeping your elbows moderately tucked.
Lightly touch the chest, then press the bar up and back toward your face until your arms are fully extended.
Lock out, reset, and repeat for the prescribed reps with a spotter for heavy loads.
formCues: Keep the bench angle moderate to bias the upper chest over the front delts
Maintain retracted shoulder blades and a proud chest
Press in a slight backward arc, not straight up over the shoulders
commonMistakes: Setting the incline too steep, turning it into a shoulder press
Lowering the bar too high onto the throat or neck
Letting the elbows flare excessively

name: Dumbbell Bench Press
instructions: Sit on the end of a flat bench with a dumbbell resting on each thigh, then lie back, using your thighs to kick the dumbbells up to chest level.
Position the dumbbells at the sides of your chest with palms facing forward, shoulder blades retracted, and feet flat on the floor.
Press both dumbbells up and slightly inward until your arms are fully extended over your chest, without clanging them together.
Lower the dumbbells under control until they are level with or slightly below your chest, feeling a stretch across the pecs.
Press back up to the top and repeat. At the end of the set, lower the dumbbells to your thighs and sit up to set them down safely.
formCues: Keep your wrists stacked over your elbows during the press
Lower until you feel a comfortable chest stretch, not pain
Keep your shoulder blades pinned to the bench
commonMistakes: Letting the dumbbells drift too far apart or too far back
Using too much weight and losing control at the bottom
Clanging the dumbbells together at the top and breaking tension

name: Incline Dumbbell Press
instructions: Set an adjustable bench to about 30 to 45 degrees and sit with a dumbbell on each thigh.
Lie back while kicking the dumbbells up to shoulder level, palms facing forward and shoulder blades retracted.
Press both dumbbells up and slightly together until your arms are fully extended over your upper chest.
Lower under control until the dumbbells are at chest level and you feel a stretch across the upper pecs.
Press back to the top and repeat, then return the dumbbells to your thighs safely at the end of the set.
formCues: Keep the incline moderate to target the upper chest, not the shoulders
Control the descent for a full stretch at the bottom
Drive your feet into the floor for stability
commonMistakes: Choosing too steep an angle and shifting load to the delts
Bouncing or rushing the bottom of the rep
Letting the elbows drop far behind the body and straining the shoulders

name: Dumbbell Chest Fly
instructions: Lie flat on a bench holding a dumbbell in each hand, pressed up over your chest with palms facing each other.
Keep a soft, fixed bend in your elbows and retract your shoulder blades.
Open your arms out to the sides in a wide arc, lowering the dumbbells until you feel a stretch across your chest, with your elbows roughly level with the bench.
Squeeze your chest to bring the dumbbells back up along the same arc until they meet over your chest.
Repeat for the prescribed reps, keeping the elbow angle constant throughout.
formCues: Move only at the shoulder, keeping the elbow bend fixed
Imagine hugging a large tree on the way up
Stop the stretch before any shoulder discomfort
commonMistakes: Bending and straightening the elbows, turning it into a press
Going too heavy and overstretching the shoulder joint
Lowering the dumbbells far below bench level

name: Cable Crossover
instructions: Set both pulleys to or above shoulder height, attach single handles, and grab one in each hand.
Step forward into a staggered stance with a slight forward lean and a soft bend in your elbows.
Start with your arms open and out to the sides, feeling a stretch across the chest.
Bring both handles down and together in front of your body in a wide arc, squeezing your chest as your hands meet.
Slowly return to the open starting position under control and repeat.
formCues: Keep a slight constant bend in the elbows throughout
Lead the motion with your hands meeting at the midline
Maintain a stable torso lean and a braced core
commonMistakes: Turning the movement into a triceps pressdown by straightening the arms
Using momentum and swinging the torso
Shrugging the shoulders up toward the ears

name: Push-Up
instructions: Start in a high plank with your hands slightly wider than shoulder width and fingers pointing forward.
Brace your core and squeeze your glutes so your body forms a straight line from head to heels.
Bend your elbows to lower your chest toward the floor, keeping your elbows at roughly a 45 degree angle to your torso.
Lower until your chest is just above the floor, then press through your hands to push back up to the start.
Fully extend your arms at the top without sagging the hips, and repeat. Drop to your knees if you cannot keep a straight line.
formCues: Keep a rigid straight line from head to heels
Tuck your elbows toward a 45 degree angle, not flared to 90
Keep your neck neutral by looking slightly ahead of your hands
commonMistakes: Sagging or piking the hips instead of holding a plank
Doing partial reps that do not lower the chest near the floor
Flaring the elbows straight out to the sides

name: Chest Dip
instructions: Grip parallel dip bars and support your bodyweight with your arms locked out at the top.
Lean your torso forward, bend your knees, and cross your ankles to emphasize the chest.
Lower yourself under control by bending the elbows, allowing them to flare slightly outward as your chest descends.
Descend until your upper arms are about parallel to the floor and you feel a stretch across the chest, without going so deep that the shoulders feel strained.
Press back up by driving through the chest and triceps until your arms are fully extended, and repeat.
formCues: Maintain a forward torso lean to bias the chest over the triceps
Keep your shoulders down and away from your ears
Control the descent rather than dropping fast
commonMistakes: Staying too upright, which shifts the work to the triceps
Descending too deep and overstretching the shoulders
Using a jerky, bouncing tempo at the bottom
